steps.description: Load the raw integer gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 6 samples, salmon quantification on Ensembl Danio rerio annotation) from counts.csv and the sample table from metadata.csv (6 rows, condition column encoding 3 treated vs 3 control). Filter out genes with counts below 10 in fewer than 3 samples. Fit DESeq2 with design ~condition (no batch term needed — single batch, unpaired). Report counts of DEGs at padj<0.05 and additionally at padj<0.05 & |log2FC|>1. Produce diagnostic plots: PCA of vst-transformed counts colored by condition, sample-distance heatmap, dispersion plot, MA plot, and a volcano plot (EnhancedVolcano). Save the full DE table and vst-normalized count matrix as CSV artifacts for downstream enrichment steps.

steps.description: Extend interpretation of the zebrafish DE result using curated human pathway databases, since no zebrafish-specific curated pathway collection (WikiPathways/Hallmark) is staged in this environment. Map the zebrafish gene symbols in the T1S1 DE table to human ortholog symbols offline using the babelgene package. Before mapping, confirm Danio rerio is present in babelgene::species(); if it is not, report that this step could not be run and that the native GO results from T2S1 remain the primary pathway output. Collapse many-to-one ortholog mappings by retaining, per human symbol, the zebrafish gene with the smallest DE p-value. Report the fraction of tested zebrafish genes that map to a 1:1 human ortholog (mapping-rate caveat). Run ORA (on DEGs at padj<0.05) and pre-ranked GSEA (on the full ortholog-mapped ranked list, ranked by DESeq2 statistic) using fgsea against the staged WikiPathways human gene sets and MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets. Report enriched pathways at adjusted p<0.05 with leading-edge genes, explicitly flagged as a cross-species proxy result contingent on ortholog-mapping quality, secondary to the zebrafish-native GO output.
acceptance_criteria: Ortholog mapping rate (1:1 human orthologs / total tested genes) is reported
ORA and GSEA tables produced against WikiPathways human and MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets, or an explicit no-run report if babelgene lacks zebrafish support
Results are clearly labeled as cross-species-proxy, not zebrafish-native

plan.title: Zebrafish drug-exposure DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The data is a bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12000 genes x 6 samples) from whole zebrafish (Danio rerio) larvae, 3 treated vs 3 control pools, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon counts on Ensembl annotation. The design supports a standard DESeq2 Wald test (~condition) without batch correction. For pathway interpretation, the environment has no zebrafish-specific curated pathway GMT (WikiPathways is staged only for human/mouse/rat, and no zebrafish KEGG/Reactome GMT was found in the managed reference census), but org.Dr.eg.db (zebrafish GO annotation) is installed and lets clusterProfiler run organism-native GO enrichment without any cross-species proxy — this is the primary, authoritative pathway-level result. To also surface curated pathway context (WikiPathways, MSigDB Hallmark), zebrafish genes are mapped to human orthologs offline via the babelgene package (bundled ortholog tables, no internet dependency) before running fgsea against the staged human WikiPathways and MSigDB Hallmark gene sets; this is explicitly flagged as a cross-species proxy result, secondary to the native GO output. The plan therefore has three steps: (1) DESeq2 differential expression producing the DE table and diagnostics, (2) organism-native GO enrichment (ORA + GSEA) via org.Dr.eg.db, and (3) ortholog-mapped enrichment against human WikiPathways/Hallmark gene sets as supplementary context.
